overview: ioneer is an ASX-listed (and NASDAQ ADR-listed as IONR) pre-production mineral developer whose sole asset is the 100%-owned Rhyolite Ridge lithium-boron project in Esmeralda County, Nevada, USA. The project is fully permitted (Record of Decision issued October 2024) and is targeted to become the first new domestically-sourced, integrated lithium-boron operation in the United States, producing battery-grade lithium carbonate/hydroxide alongside boric acid. The company earns no operating revenue; it is funded by equity raisings, a US$996 million U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) loan facility, and is seeking a strategic equity partner before taking a Final Investment Decision (FID), targeted for second half of 2026, with first production guided for 2029.

business_model.summary: Pre-revenue project developer. 'Business model' is project economics and financing path rather than existing sales: ioneer's value is the net present value of a single mine/processing complex, monetized only once construction is funded and the plant reaches production. Capital intensity is financed through a layered stack: DOE debt (~US$996m), an incoming equity/strategic partner stake (previously structured as a 50% JV with Sibanye-Stillwater, which exited February 2025; current plan is to sell a smaller ~40% stake), periodic institutional equity placements (A$72m / ~US$50m completed January/February 2026), and a US SEC Form F-3 shelf registration filed in 2026 for future debt/equity issuance.
business_model.customer_type: Future B2B offtake with battery material and chemical companies (binding offtake/distribution agreements already signed for boric acid; lithium carbonate offtake framework in place subject to FID conditions precedent)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% single-asset exposure: Rhyolite Ridge, Nevada, USA. Corporate listing/reporting in Australia (ASX) with a USD functional currency from FY2023 onward and a US-based operating subsidiary structure.

main_competitors: Lithium Americas Corp. (Thacker Pass, Nevada — also DOE/GM-backed, targeting 2027 first production)
Albemarle Corporation (Silver Peak, Nevada brine; global lithium leader)
Rio Tinto (Jadar lithium-borate project, Serbia — paused; also the dominant global borates producer via U.S. Borax)
U.S. Borax / Eti Maden (incumbent global boron/borate suppliers)
Chinese/South American lithium incumbents (SQM, Albemarle, Ganfeng, Tianqi) supplying the bulk of global lithium chemicals
competitive_position.market_position: Pre-production developer with no current market share. Positioning rests on being described by management as 'the only permitted, shovel-ready lithium-boron project in the U.S.' and one of the few U.S. lithium projects with closed DOE debt financing, alongside Thacker Pass.

moat_factors.description: Full federal/state permits in hand (BLM Record of Decision, Nevada water/air permits) after a ~4-5 year NEPA process that competitors would need to replicate; recently upheld by U.S. District Court (March 2026), though under appeal.
Only known economic lithium-boron deposit in the U.S.; boric acid co-product revenue is credited against costs, supporting a stated AISC of ~US$4,628/t LCE (low-cost quartile) net of boron credits.

moat_factors.factor: U.S. government financing and policy tailwind
moat_factors.description: US$996m DOE loan already closed; boron added to the U.S. critical minerals list (Nov 2025); conditional award for a U.S. Army land lease at Tooele, Utah for a critical-minerals processing facility.
77-year mine plan, 548Mt total mineral resource, 266Mt ore reserve (as of Dec 2025), providing long-dated optionality and expansion potential (resource open to north/south/east).
No operating track record; not a scale advantage versus established producers (Albemarle, SQM, Rio Tinto) who have existing customer relationships and balance sheets.

weaknesses: Single-asset concentration — all value depends on one project reaching FID and then construction without major cost/schedule overruns
No current revenue or production; entirely reliant on external financing and project completion
Lost its original 50% equity partner (Sibanye-Stillwater) in February 2025 on lithium price concerns and is still searching for a replacement, with repeated timeline slippage through 2026
Small market capitalization (~A$300m / ~US$200m as of November 2026) relative to the scale of capital required to build the project
Subject to active Ninth Circuit appeal litigation over its environmental permits, creating residual legal/headline risk even after a favorable district court ruling

growth_drivers: Securing a strategic equity partner to satisfy DOE loan conditions precedent and enable a positive Final Investment Decision (targeted 2H 2026); non-binding MOUs signed with South Korea's KIND and Hyundai Engineering in mid-2026

Process improvements (vat leach retention time cut from 3 days to 1.5 days) that increased unlevered project NPV 64% to ~US$2.23bn and IRR by 350bps to 18.0%, with minimal extra capex — ongoing technical optimization could add further upside

U.S. critical minerals policy tailwinds: boron added to the U.S. critical minerals list (Nov 2025), Trump administration proclamation on critical minerals (Jan 2026), and a conditional U.S. Army land lease at Tooele, Utah for a defense-related processing facility
Advancing the onsite lithium hydroxide circuit to Year 3 of operations (from Year 4), improving capital efficiency and realized pricing versus carbonate-only sales
EcoPro Innovation lithium-clay R&D collaboration (process flow sheet completed early 2026) as a potential adjacent growth avenue beyond Rhyolite Ridge
Defense-grade boron carbide pre-feasibility study, opening a potential higher-value, non-battery boron product line
Long-dated resource (77-year mine life, resource open on three sides) supporting potential future expansion beyond the initial Stage 1 design

business.description: FID and construction depend on securing a strategic equity partner; the process has slipped repeatedly through 2025-2026 (now targeted end-September/2H 2026) with no binding agreement yet signed as of the latest disclosures.
Project has not yet reached FID; once construction begins, Stage 1 build-out carries typical large mining-project cost overrun and schedule risk before first production (guided 2029).

Existing boric acid offtake/distribution agreements carry conditions precedent tied to FID and first production timing; counterparties may not perform or may require renegotiation if the project is delayed.
Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve estimates are based on geological interpretation and could differ materially from actual mineralization/recoveries.

Ongoing Ninth Circuit appeal (filed April 2026) by the Center for Biological Diversity and allied groups against the BLM's Record of Decision; company does not expect delay to construction but an adverse ruling is a tail risk; decision not expected until mid-2027.

financial.description: Pre-revenue company funding ongoing losses and project capex via equity issuance (A$72m placement Jan/Feb 2026 alone added 400m shares); further capital raises likely before and even after FID, and an SEC Form F-3 shelf has been filed to facilitate additional U.S. debt/equity issuance.

Net cash of only ~US$58.8m at 30 June 2026 against a project requiring well over US$1bn of total capital; DOE loan first-advance is conditional on closing a strategic partnership, securing additional funding, and a project finance model bring-down — any of which could be delayed.
Reports in USD since FY2023 but equity raised and listed primarily in AUD on the ASX, creating basis risk between financing currency and functional/reporting currency.

regulatory.description: Despite a fully issued federal Record of Decision and a favorable March 2026 district court ruling, the project remains under active appeal; environmental groups have a long history of litigating this project over the endangered Tiehm's buckwheat plant.

Company flags risk from potential changes in U.S. federal administration and shifting climate/critical-minerals policy; DOE loan terms were negotiated under a specific policy environment that could change.

macro.description: Project economics (NPV, IRR) are highly sensitive to long-term lithium price assumptions; Sibanye-Stillwater's 2025 exit was explicitly attributed to weak lithium prices failing to clear its investment hurdle rate.
AISC guidance of ~US$4,628/t LCE is stated net of boric acid revenue credits; a weaker boron price environment would raise effective lithium production costs.
Large fixed-rate DOE loan facility and ongoing reliance on capital markets make the project's cost of capital and equity raising capacity sensitive to broader rate conditions.
Long-term lithium demand, and thus project value, depends on the pace of global EV adoption and battery/stationary storage buildout.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Mainstream 2026 forecasts cluster around US$15,000-25,000/t for battery-grade lithium carbonate, with views split between a near-term surplus (S&P Global flags ~109kt 2026 surplus) and a structural longer-term deficit (IEA sees 2035 mine supply covering only ~60% of stated-policy demand). U.S. policy is increasingly supportive of domestic lithium and (newly) boron supply chains, benefiting projects like Rhyolite Ridge and Lithium Americas' Thacker Pass (also DOE/GM-backed, first production guided 2027).
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — commodity-price and capital-markets cyclical; project valuation and the ability to raise equity both swing with lithium price sentiment, as demonstrated by Sibanye-Stillwater's 2025 exit.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate to high — large project financing stack (DOE debt plus future equity/debt raises) is sensitive to the cost and availability of capital.

guidance.management_commentary: Executive Chair James Calaway described 2026 as a potential 'transformational step' toward realizing Rhyolite Ridge's economic potential, citing favorable U.S. government policy trends on critical minerals (boron's addition to the critical minerals list, Trump administration proclamation) and reiterating confidence in the company's legal position on the pending Ninth Circuit appeal, which it does not expect to delay construction.

bull_case: Fully permitted, 'shovel-ready' status with a favorable March 2026 district court ruling removes much of the regulatory risk that sidelines most U.S. mining projects, and gives Rhyolite Ridge first-mover advantage as the only permitted U.S. lithium-boron project
US$996m DOE loan already closed (not merely conditional) provides a large committed low-cost debt tranche once conditions precedent are satisfied, reducing the equity capital needed to reach FID

Recent technical improvements (1.5-day leach) lifted unlevered NPV 64% to ~US$2.23bn and IRR to 18% with minimal extra capex, showing a credible path to further economic upside through ongoing optimization

Strong and strengthening U.S. policy tailwinds (boron added to critical minerals list, presidential proclamation, conditional U.S. Army land lease at Tooele) support both financing and potential customer/government demand

Non-binding MOUs with Korean partners KIND and Hyundai Engineering suggest the strategic partnering process, while delayed, has credible counterparties in late-stage discussion ahead of a targeted 2H 2026 FID
bear_case: Strategic partner search has repeatedly slipped (originally four months in 2025, pushed through H1 2026 and then to end-September 2026) with no binding agreement signed as of the latest disclosures — the project cannot reach FID or draw the DOE loan without it

Sibanye-Stillwater's February 2025 exit, explicitly citing weak lithium prices failing its investment hurdle, is a precedent that a soft lithium price environment could again deter a new equity partner or compress the terms ioneer can negotiate (now seeking to sell only ~40% versus the prior 50%)

Persistent cash burn and a project needing well over US$1bn in total capital against only ~US$59m of net cash (30 June 2026) point to continued, likely large, shareholder dilution regardless of partner outcome

Single-asset, pre-revenue structure means any construction delay, cost overrun, or adverse Ninth Circuit ruling (decision not expected until mid-2027) could materially impair the investment case with no offsetting cash-generating business to cushion the blow
Even after FID, first production is not guided until 2029, implying several more years of financing risk, execution risk, and commodity-price exposure before any revenue materializes
